## Functions

### `ConsentBanner`

```ts
ConsentBanner(props: ConsentBannerProps): Html
```

Asks once whether analytics may run, and runs them only after a yes.

Rendered `hidden`: consent.js shows it to a visitor who has not chosen,
loads `loaders` on Accept (and on later visits while the choice stands),
and on Reject withdraws — `gtag('consent', 'update', …denied)` and
`clarity('consent', false)` when present, the trackers' cookies
expired. `[data-consent-open]` anywhere (a "Cookie settings" link)
shows it again with focus on its first button; `consent:change`
(`detail: { state, key }`) bubbles from it on every choice. Without a
script nothing loads and nothing is asked. CSP-clean: the loaders are
data attributes, never inline script.

## Types

### `ConsentLoader`

A script to load once the visitor accepts — a tracker's loader.

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src` | `string` | yes | The script URL. Under a strict CSP its origin must be in `script-src`. |
| `async` | `boolean` |  | Load without blocking the next loader (`gtag/js`). @default false — loaders run in order |
| `attrs` | `Readonly` |  | Attributes the loader reads (`data-id`, `data-path`) and `integrity` / `crossorigin`. Event-handler attributes (`on*`) are refused. |

### `ConsentBannerProps`

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` |  | The banner's id — what `[data-consent-open="#consent"]` targets. @default "consent" |
| `title` | `string | Html` | yes | The question, e.g. "Cookies for analytics?" |
| `body` | `string | Html` | yes | What is collected, by whom, and where to read more. |
| `accept` | `string` |  | The Accept button's text. @default "Accept" |
| `reject` | `string` |  | The Reject button's text. @default "Reject" |
| `variant` | `ButtonVariant` |  | Both buttons wear the same variant: refusing is as easy and as prominent as accepting, and nothing is pre-ticked. @default "primary" |
| `loaders` | `typeOperator` |  | Loaded, in order, after Accept — and on every later visit while the choice stands. |
| `storageKey` | `string` |  | Where the choice is kept (`granted` \| `denied`) in localStorage — in the browser, so every visitor gets the same cached page. @default "ui-consent" |
| `cookies` | `typeOperator` |  | Cookies expired on Reject, on the host and every parent domain; a trailing `*` matches a prefix. @default Google Analytics and Microsoft Clarity's: `_ga*`, `_gid`, `_gat*`, `_clck`, `_clsk` |
| `attrs` | `Attrs` |  |  |

## Usage

Each example as the rAPId call and the HTML it renders — the markup a plain page writes by hand. Icons are inline SVG in the real output; they are shortened to `<svg …>…</svg>` here.

### Analytics only after Accept

Rendered hidden: consent.js shows it to a visitor who has not chosen and loads the scripts only after Accept. A `[data-consent-open]` link anywhere reopens it.

```ts
html`${
  ConsentBanner({
    title: "Cookies for analytics?",
    body: html`We would use Google Analytics to see which pages help. <a href="/privacy">Privacy notice</a>`,
    loaders: [
      { src: "https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtag/js?id=G-XXXX", async: true },
      { src: "/public/ga.js", attrs: { "data-id": "G-XXXX" } },
    ],
    storageKey: "acme-consent",
  })
}<a href="#" data-consent-open>Cookie settings</a>`
```

```html
<div class="consent" id="consent" role="region" aria-labelledby="consent-title" data-consent="" data-consent-key="acme-consent" data-consent-loaders="[{&quot;src&quot;:&quot;https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtag/js?id=G-XXXX&quot;,&quot;async&quot;:true},{&quot;src&quot;:&quot;/public/ga.js&quot;,&quot;attrs&quot;:{&quot;data-id&quot;:&quot;G-XXXX&quot;}}]" hidden="">
  <div class="consent__card">
    <div class="consent__text">
      <p class="consent__title" id="consent-title">Cookies for analytics?</p>
      <div class="consent__body">
        We would use Google Analytics to see which pages help.
        <a href="/privacy">Privacy notice</a>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="consent__actions">
      <button type="button" class="btn" data-consent-accept="">Accept</button>
      <button type="button" class="btn" data-consent-reject="">Reject</button>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
<a href="#" data-consent-open>Cookie settings</a>
```

## CSS hooks

Classes defined by `components/consent/consent.css` — structural, token-driven; override from an unlayered stylesheet (see [Theming](../UI-Theming.md)):

`.consent`, `.consent__actions`, `.consent__body`, `.consent__card`, `.consent__text`, `.consent__title`

## Behaviour

`components/consent/consent.js` ships in `ui.js` (delegated on `document`, re-initialised after a rAPId swap).

Attributes it reads or writes: `data-consent`, `data-consent-accept`, `data-consent-cookies`, `data-consent-key`, `data-consent-loaders`, `data-consent-open`, `data-consent-ready`, `data-consent-reject`.

Events: `consent:change`, `rapid:swapped`.
